title.zh: 子午流注养生法：十二时辰养生全攻略

description.zh: 深入解读中医子午流注理论，掌握十二时辰养生方法，让身体与自然节律同步
description.en: Deep dive into TCM's Midnight-Noon Flow theory, master the 12-meridian daily wellness method

zh.text: 子午流注是中医理论中独具特色的一门时间医学，它揭示了一个深刻的规律：人体气血在一天24小时内并非均匀分布，而是按照固定的节律依次流经十二经脉。每个时辰（两小时）都有一条对应的经络当令值班，气血在该时辰最为旺盛。《针灸大成》对子午流注针法有系统的论述，其核心思想可追溯到《黄帝内经》"天人相应"的哲学——人体这个小宇宙与天地大宇宙之间存在着节律上的共振与同步。所谓"子午"，指的是时辰中的子时（23时至1时）和午时（11时至13时），分别代表阴之极和阳之极；而"流注"则形象地描述了气血如水流般依次灌注经脉的动态过程。
十二时辰经络养生详解
子时是一天中阴气最盛、阳气初生的时刻，对应胆经当令。《素问·五脏别论》说："凡十一脏，取决于胆也。"胆气的生发关系到次日全身脏腑的功能状态。此时若已安然入睡，则胆气得以升发，胆汁推陈出新。反之，如果子时还在熬夜，那么初生的阳气被耗损，胆气不升，第二天就会出现口苦、精神不振、决策力下降等问题。我常对患者说："过了晚上11点还不睡，不是在熬夜，是在熬胆气。"建议23点前入睡，以养初生之阳气。
丑时气血流注肝经，肝脏在此时间段进行解毒和藏血工作。《素问·五脏生成》曰："人卧则血归于肝。"人在深度睡眠时，大量血液回归肝脏进行净化，然后将新鲜血液重新输布全身。如果此时失眠或浅睡易醒，肝脏的解毒功能会大打折扣。临床上很多肝功能异常的患者都有长期熬夜史，而面部色斑、暗沉也与肝经当令时得不到休息密切相关。侧卧姿势有利于肝经气血的顺畅运行，建议在此时间段保证深度睡眠。

寅时是肺经最活跃的时段，肺朝百脉、主治节，将肝经净化后的气血输布到全身各处。中医讲"肺为华盖"，位居脏腑最高处，好比一个调度中心。这个时间段如果自然醒来且难以再次入睡，往往是肺气不足的表现，肺的宣发肃降功能失常。秋冬季节咳嗽气喘的患者常在此时症状加重，这正是"寅时肺旺"的体现。我的建议是：如果寅时自然醒来，不必勉强再睡，可以静卧做腹式深呼吸，帮助肺气宣发。但一般不建议寅时早起锻炼，因气血刚刚开始输布，过早活动不利于阳气的平稳升发。
卯时大肠经气血最旺，是排便的最佳时段。《灵枢·经脉》记载大肠经"主津液所生病"，大肠的主要功能是传导糟粕、吸收水分。早晨起床后先喝一杯温开水，可以刺激肠胃蠕动，促进排便。久而久之形成习惯，对预防便秘和肠道疾病非常有益。很多坚持卯时排便的人，不仅肠道功能好，皮肤也干净透亮——因为"肺与大肠相表里"，肠道通畅则肺气肃降，皮肤自然会好。
辰时胃经当令，这个时间段胃的消化吸收能力达到一天中的峰值，所以早餐一定要吃好。中医强调"胃为水谷之海"，辰时进食最有利于营养的摄取和转化。很多为了节食而不吃早餐的人，实际上是在逆天而行——胃气最旺之时不给它提供"原料"，不仅伤胃，还会导致胆汁淤积，长期下来胆囊疾病、胃病的风险都会增加。早餐宜温热、营养均衡，包含碳水、蛋白质和优质脂肪，尽量避免冰冷食物直接刺激胃腑。
巳时是脾经值班的时段，脾主运化，将胃消化后的食物精微转化为气血输送到全身。巳时人体精力充沛，是工作学习的黄金时间。脾虚的人在这个时间段常常感到困倦乏力，这提示脾的运化功能不足。对于这类人，我建议适度活动四肢，"脾主四肢"，活动可以反过来刺激脾的功能。同时避免久坐，久坐伤脾——很多上班族越坐越累，就是因为脾阳被压抑。此时可喝一杯温热的健脾茶，如黄芪红枣茶。
午时是心经当令的时段，也是阳气最盛开始转阴的关键时刻。心为"君主之官"，主血脉和神志。午时小憩15至30分钟，可以养心安神，为下午的工作充电。午睡最好以"子午觉"的形式进行——即午时（11-13点）闭目养神即可，不一定要沉睡。即使无法入睡，闭眼静坐15分钟，让心神收敛片刻，效果也远胜于继续工作。中医讲"心藏神"，午时养神即养心。需要注意的是，午时不宜剧烈运动或暴饮暴食，以免耗伤心气。
未时小肠经当令，小肠的主要功能是"分清泌浊"——将经过脾胃初步消化的食物进一步分解，吸收精微物质，输送到各脏腑，将糟粕下送大肠。这个时间段人体的吸收能力较好，午餐的营养在此阶段得到充分吸收。建议午餐在12:30至13:00之间吃完，给胃和小肠留出足够的消化时间。未时多喝水也有利于代谢废物的排出。
申时是膀胱经最旺的时段。膀胱经是人体最长、穴位最多的经脉，从头部贯穿背部直达足部。膀胱经当令时，气血充足，大脑供血良好，因此申时被认为是一天中记忆力最强的时段，适合学习、背诵、处理复杂事务。对于学生和脑力工作者来说，这个时间段应充分利用。同时膀胱经主水液代谢，申时要注意及时补充水分、适当排小便，避免憋尿。久坐办公室的人，在申时站起来活动一下，拍打后背膀胱经区域，对缓解腰部疲劳非常有益。
酉时肾经气血最旺，是补肾的最佳时间。肾为"先天之本"，主藏精、主纳气。酉时正值日落时分，阳气开始潜藏，阴气渐长，与肾脏"主蛰藏"的特性相吻合。这个时间段适合进行适度的体育锻炼——散步、太极拳、八段锦等，以微微出汗为度，不宜大汗淋漓以免耗伤肾精。晚餐宜清淡，避免过于油腻和过咸的食物，因咸味入肾，过咸反而伤肾。可以在酉时用温水泡脚15至20分钟，刺激足底涌泉穴，有引火归元、补肾安神之效。
戌时心包经当令。心包是心脏的外围保护组织，"代心受邪"，《灵枢·邪客》说："诸邪之在于心者，皆在于心之包络。"这个时间段是一天中放松心情的最佳时段。心包经旺时，适宜散步、听音乐、与家人朋友聊天，做一些让自己心情愉悦的事情。尽量避免在这个时间段争吵、讨论焦虑的话题或进行剧烈运动。戌时按摩心包经——从肘窝沿手臂内侧中线向手掌方向按揉，对缓解胸闷、心烦有立竿见影的效果。

亥时三焦经当令，也是一天中最后一个时辰。三焦是通行元气和水液的通道，三焦通则全身通。《难经·六十六难》指出："三焦者，原气之别使也，主通行三气，经历于五脏六腑。"亥时是准备入眠、过渡到新一天的关键时段。此时应用温水泡脚，听舒缓的音乐，放下手机和电脑，让身心逐渐安静下来。亥时是"阴阳交替"的过渡期，此时不宜进行刺激性活动，否则会干扰阴阳交接的正常节律。如果能做到在亥时放松、子时入睡，就是最顺应天时的作息方式。
子午流注的核心养生原则

子午流注养生法的核心可以概括为四句话：顺天时而动，应天时而静，食饮有节，起居有常。具体来说，一是规律作息是基础——人体的生物钟与十二时辰的节律高度吻合，不规律的生活是最伤气血的；二是按时进食、七分饱为宜，辰时（早餐）要吃好、午时（午餐）要吃饱、酉时（晚餐）要吃少；三是不同时辰调整活动强度——卯时至巳时宜活动、午时宜静养、酉时至戌时宜适度运动；四是保持情志平稳，辰时心气旺盛要保持积极心态，戌时心包经旺要学会放松，避免在亥时心绪不宁影响睡眠。此外，根据不同时辰按摩相应对经络的关键穴位，可以增强养生效果——如卯时大肠经按揉合谷、曲池，辰时胃经按揉足三里，午时心经按揉神门，酉时肾经按揉涌泉、太溪。
温馨提示：子午流注养生需要长期坚持才能见效。每个人的体质不同，应根据自身情况调整养生方案。如有健康问题，请咨询专业中医师。

en.text: Midnight-Noon Flow (Zi Wu Liu Zhu) is a unique chronomedicine theory in Traditional Chinese Medicine. It reveals a profound principle: Qi and Blood do not flow uniformly throughout the 24-hour day but circulate through the twelve meridians in a fixed rhythm. Each two-hour period (Shi Chen) corresponds to a specific meridian that is at its peak. The Dacheng of Acupuncture (Zhenjiu Dacheng) systematically discusses Midnight-Noon Flow acupuncture, with its core thought tracing back to the "Unity of Man and Nature" philosophy in the Huangdi Neijing — there exists a rhythmic resonance between the human microcosm and the macrocosm of heaven and earth. "Zi" refers to the Zi period (11 PM-1 AM) of maximum Yin, and "Wu" refers to the Wu period (11 AM-1 PM) of maximum Yang. "Liu Zhu" vividly describes Qi and Blood flowing through meridians like a stream of water.
The 12 Meridians in the Daily Cycle
Zi Period (23:00-01:00) — Gallbladder Meridian

Zi is the period of maximum Yin when Yang Qi is just beginning to be born, corresponding to the Gallbladder meridian. The Suwen states: "All eleven organs depend on the Gallbladder." The rising of Gallbladder Qi affects the functional state of all organs the following day. If one is peacefully asleep at this time, Gallbladder Qi rises properly and bile is renewed. Conversely, staying awake during Zi period depletes the nascent Yang Qi — the next day one experiences bitter taste, low energy, and poor decision-making. I often tell patients: "Staying up past 11 PM isn't just staying up late — you're draining your Gallbladder Qi." It is recommended to be asleep before 11 PM to nurture the newborn Yang energy.
Chou Period (01:00-03:00) — Liver Meridian

During Chou period, Qi and Blood flow through the Liver meridian, and the Liver performs detoxification and blood storage. The Suwen states: "When a person lies down, blood returns to the Liver." During deep sleep, a large volume of blood returns to the Liver for cleansing and is then redistributed. If one experiences insomnia or light sleep during this period, the Liver's detoxification function is compromised. Clinically, many patients with abnormal liver function have a history of chronic late nights. Facial pigmentation and dull complexion are also closely related to lack of rest during the Liver meridian's peak hours. Sleeping on the side facilitates smooth Qi and Blood flow through the Liver meridian.
Yin Period (03:00-05:00) — Lung Meridian

Yin period is when the Lung meridian is most active. The Lung faces the hundred vessels and governs regulation, distributing the purified Qi and Blood from the Liver to the entire body. Called the "canopy" of the body, the Lung sits above all other organs like a command center. If one naturally wakes during this period and cannot fall back asleep, it often indicates Lung Qi deficiency with impaired dispersion and descension function. Patients with cough and asthma frequently experience worsening symptoms during this period. My advice: if you wake naturally during Yin period, there is no need to force more sleep. Lie still and practice deep abdominal breathing to assist Lung Qi dispersion. However, early morning vigorous exercise is not recommended, as Qi and Blood are only beginning to circulate.
Mao Period (05:00-07:00) — Large Intestine Meridian

During Mao period, the Large Intestine meridian is at its peak — the optimal time for bowel movements. The Lingshu records that the Large Intestine meridian governs fluid-related disorders. The Large Intestine's main function is transmitting waste and absorbing water. Drinking a glass of warm water upon rising stimulates intestinal peristalsis and promotes defecation. Establishing a habit of morning bowel movements is highly beneficial for preventing constipation and intestinal diseases. Those who maintain this practice often have not only good intestinal function but also clear, radiant skin — because the Lung and Large Intestine are internally-externally paired; when the intestine is unobstructed, Lung Qi descends properly and the skin naturally improves.
Chen Period (07:00-09:00) — Stomach Meridian

During Chen period, the Stomach meridian is at its peak, making the Stomach's digestive and absorptive capacity optimal for the day. This is why breakfast must be substantial and nutritious. TCM emphasizes that the Stomach is the "sea of food and drink." Eating during Chen period maximizes nutrient intake and transformation. Those who skip breakfast to lose weight are working against nature — when Stomach Qi is at its strongest, not providing it with "raw materials" not only injures the Stomach but also causes bile stasis. Over time, the risk of gallbladder and gastric diseases increases. Breakfast should be warm, nutritionally balanced with carbohydrates, protein, and quality fats, avoiding cold foods.
Si Period (09:00-11:00) — Spleen Meridian

During Si period, the Spleen meridian is on duty. The Spleen governs transportation and transformation, converting the digested food essence from the Stomach into Qi and Blood for distribution throughout the body. This is the golden period for work and study, as the body is fully energized. Spleen-deficient individuals often feel drowsy and fatigued during this period. For such people, I recommend moderate limb activity — "the Spleen governs the limbs," and movement stimulates Spleen function. Prolonged sitting should be avoided as it suppresses Spleen Yang. Many office workers feel increasingly tired the longer they sit because Spleen Yang is being suppressed. A warm Spleen-tonifying tea such as astragalus and red date tea is beneficial.
Wu Period (11:00-13:00) — Heart Meridian

During Wu period, the Heart meridian is on duty. This is also the critical moment when Yang reaches its maximum and begins to turn toward Yin. The Heart is the "monarch organ," governing blood vessels and consciousness. A 15-30 minute nap during Wu period nourishes the Heart and calms the spirit, recharging energy for the afternoon. Even if unable to sleep, sitting quietly with eyes closed for 15 minutes to let the spirit settle is far more beneficial than continuing to work. TCM teaches that "the Heart houses the spirit" — nourishing the spirit at midday nourishes the Heart. Vigorous exercise or overeating during Wu period should be avoided, as they deplete Heart Qi.
Wei Period (13:00-15:00) — Small Intestine Meridian

During Wei period, the Small Intestine meridian is active. The Small Intestine's main function is "separating pure from impure" — further breaking down food that has been initially digested by the Spleen and Stomach, absorbing the essence, and sending waste to the Large Intestine. The body's absorptive capacity is excellent during this period. Lunch is recommended between 12:30 and 1:00 PM to allow sufficient digestive time. Drinking adequate water during Wei period also facilitates waste elimination.
Shen Period (15:00-17:00) — Bladder Meridian

During Shen period, the Bladder meridian is at its peak. The Bladder meridian is the longest meridian with the most acupoints, running from the head through the entire back down to the feet. When the Bladder meridian is at its peak, Qi and Blood are ample and cerebral blood supply is optimal — making this the period of strongest memory, ideal for studying, memorization, and handling complex tasks. Students and knowledge workers should make full use of this time. The Bladder also governs fluid metabolism; adequate water intake and timely urination are important to avoid urine retention. Office workers should stand up and gently pat the Bladder meridian area along the back to relieve lower back fatigue.
You Period (17:00-19:00) — Kidney Meridian

During You period, Kidney meridian Qi and Blood are at their peak — the best time for Kidney tonification. The Kidney is the "congenital foundation," storing Essence and governing Qi reception. You period coincides with sunset, when Yang Qi begins to hide and Yin Qi gradually grows, matching the Kidney's nature of "storage and closure." Moderate exercise such as walking, Tai Chi, or Ba Duan Jin is appropriate during this time — aim for mild perspiration, avoiding profuse sweating which depletes Kidney Essence. Dinner should be light, avoiding excessively greasy or salty foods (salt enters the Kidney, but excess salt injures it). Soaking feet in warm water for 15-20 minutes during You period stimulates Yongquan (KI1), guiding fire back to its source, tonifying the Kidney, and calming the spirit.
Xu Period (19:00-21:00) — Pericardium Meridian

During Xu period, the Pericardium meridian is active. The Pericardium protects the Heart, "receiving pathogens on behalf of the Heart." The Lingshu states: "All pathogens affecting the Heart lodge in the Pericardium." This is the optimal time of day for relaxation. Activities such as walking, listening to music, and chatting with family and friends are ideal. Arguments, anxiety-provoking discussions, and vigorous exercise should be avoided. Massaging the Pericardium meridian during Xu period — from the elbow fossa along the midline of the inner arm toward the palm — provides immediate relief for chest congestion and irritability.
Hai Period (21:00-23:00) — San Jiao Meridian

During Hai period, the San Jiao (Triple Heater) meridian is active — the last two-hour period of the day. The San Jiao is the passageway for Yuan Qi and body fluids; when San Jiao is unobstructed, the entire body is unobstructed. The Nanjing states: "The San Jiao is the envoy of Yuan Qi, governing the circulation of the three Qi through the five Zang and six Fu organs." Hai period is the critical transition time for preparing for sleep and entering the new day. Soaking feet in warm water, listening to calming music, and putting down phones and computers allows body and mind to gradually settle. Hai period is the "Yin-Yang transition" period; stimulating activities at this time disrupt the normal rhythm of Yin-Yang alternation. Mastering relaxation during Hai period and falling asleep by Zi period represents the most harmonious way of living in accordance with nature.
Core Principles of Midnight-Noon Flow Wellness

The core of Midnight-Noon Flow wellness can be summarized in four sentences: move in harmony with nature's activity phases, rest in harmony with nature's stillness phases, eat and drink with moderation, and maintain regularity in daily life. Specifically, regularity is foundational — the body's biological clock is highly synchronized with the 12-period rhythm. Irregular living is most damaging to Qi and Blood. Eat on time and stop at 70% fullness: a good breakfast during Chen period, a full lunch during Wu period, and a light dinner during You period. Adjust activity intensity by period: active during Mao to Si, rest during Wu, moderate exercise during You to Xu. Maintain emotional balance: keep a positive mindset during Chen period when Heart Qi is strong, learn to relax during Xu period when the Pericardium is active, and avoid mental agitation during Hai period that affects sleep quality. Additionally, massaging key acupoints of the corresponding meridian during each period enhances wellness effects — such as pressing Hegu and Quchi during Mao period (Large Intestine), Zusanli during Chen period (Stomach), Shenmen during Wu period (Heart), and Yongquan and Taixi during You period (Kidney).
Note: Midnight-Noon Flow wellness requires long-term practice to see results. Everyone's constitution is different, adjust accordingly. Consult a qualified TCM practitioner for health concerns.
